CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

Shared conventions

The portfolio’s shared rules are synced into .claude/shared/ from pedrobtz/packages:claude/shared/. Never edit them here. Where this file and a shared file disagree, this file wins for this package.

@.claude/shared/workflow.md @.claude/shared/r-package.md @.claude/shared/ci.md @.claude/shared/native-code.md @.claude/shared/correctness.md @.claude/shared/assurance.md

What this is

zumir brings MIR, Vladimir Makarov’s lightweight JIT compiler, to R in three ways. First, as a provider: family packages (zupmxode first) use LinkingTo: zumir and a versioned C API table to build MIR functions and get back native function pointers, or MIR’s interpreter where MIR has no code generator for the CPU. Both tiers need executable memory (design §4.4, Q5). Second, as cfunction(): R users compile a short numeric C function with MIR’s own c2mir compiler, with no Rtools, Xcode tools or gcc needed. Third, as rfunction(): a numeric R function, in the subset of design §4.6, compiled to native code that returns exactly what R returns. There are no Imports, only Suggests: testthat. MIR is vendored, and the whole package is one shared object. It is not a full C compiler, not a sandbox (user code runs with .Call()’s rights), and not a wrapper around the system toolchain the way inline and Rcpp are.

The specification is .agents/design.md, adopted from RFC 0073. It outranks this file: CLAUDE.md orients, the design decides.

Current state

Scaffolded 2026-11-13 with create-pkg.sh; no functionality yet. The roadmap in .agents/roadmap.md takes it to v0.1.0.

Stage 0, the MIR spike, ran outside this repository in pedrobtz/mirspike and decided that zumir is built (its RESULTS.md, 2026-11-13). Its harness (the three right-hand sides, the seccomp W+X test, the error loop) is the starting point for Stages 2 to 4.

Versions and dependents

The current version’s parent issue is #1 (v0.1.0). Sibling packages that depend on this one before CRAN does: zupmxode (RFC 0047), which lowers its IR to MIR through the C API.

Commands

Only the shared commands so far.

Architecture

To be written as stages land; see .agents/design.md. The scaffold set up a C native layer (src/zumir.c, registered with useDynLib).

Invariants that are easy to break

These are fixed by the design before any code exists:

  • MIR never ends the R process (D4). MIR’s default error handler calls exit(1), and MIR_init can reach it before a handler is installed. Every context gets zumir’s handler through MIR_set_error_func, the paths that run before that are patched, and every entry from R or from the table is a recovery point. A missed path kills the analyst’s session.
  • No longjmp crosses a consumer’s frames. Every zumir_ entry in the C API returns a status code, and every MIR_ entry is a shim that traps and records the error in its context, which can then only be freed (§4.3, D20). A trap set in one call never covers a later one.
  • A MIR update can break consumers’ binaries. The table carries a MIR ABI number; bump it whenever an exposed mir.h enum or struct changes (D21).
  • The C API table only grows. Its first field is the version, and later versions only append fields. Consumers compiled against an older header must keep working.
  • No exit, abort, stdout or stderr in the shared object (§11). MIR’s output goes to a buffer that becomes the R condition’s message.
  • The interpreter is not shareable across threads (D10): one interpreted function called from eight threads gave wrong answers in the spike. On that tier each thread compiles in its own context; native code is shared.
  • rfunction() answers as R does or errors (D16): every non-NaN result equals R’s bit for bit, and where matching R is not cheap it refuses. Its tests compare with R through identical(num.eq = FALSE) (#21).
  • cfunction() reads no system header (D5), and its import resolver resolves only the fixed list in D6. Anything else is a link error, so the same source behaves the same everywhere and can’t reach R’s internals.
  • MIR’s symbols are hidden from Stage 2, so they can’t clash with another package that vendors MIR.

Testing

None yet: no conformance suite, no helpers, no runtime to report. Design §8 plans MIR’s own tests, mir-tests through mir_function(), and c-tests through c2mir by the corpus’s own rules, on both tiers; .agents/assurance.md lists every oracle and its gap.

Continuous integration

The package calls pedrobtz/r-actions for R-CMD-check.yaml (profile auto) and coverage.yaml. pkgdown.yaml builds the site with r-lib/actions, and assurance.yaml calls r-actions’ assurance.yml. The roadmap marks Stages 2 to 5, 7 and 8 full, with the closing three.

Vendored native code

MIR (MIT), from vnmakarov/mir at commit dc2c763f1c8bc746102ce87933d866335f9e6c06 (master, 2026-10-23), always named by its full hash. Deviation from native-code.md: that file says to pin a stable release. D2 (the maintainer’s decision) pins this commit on purpose, because the only tag (v1.0.0, May 2024) misses two and a half years of fixes. A bump re-runs the spike’s checks. MIR goes under src/vendor/mir/, kept as upstream plus a numbered patch queue in tools/patches/, never a fork (D12). tools/vendor.sh records the commit, the file list and the patches (§4.1, §4.2). Not vendored yet: fill in the file list and every local patch when Stage 2 lands. The README’s Mozilla Public License mention is about NanoJIT, not any MIR file (spike question 7).
